status: First retained-deployment register/replace concurrency slice qualified within the stated model and native-component boundaries; HUB-REGISTER-01 and the comprehensive goal remain partial
evidence_class: Handwritten Lean transaction model with reviewed Rust/SQL mapping and separate native regression. This package is not an Aeneas extraction of async Rust or SQL and does not establish formal SQL refinement.

completed_counterexample.inputs: Parametric complete metadata, row/role payloads and disjoint frame, with unequal old/new metadata; seed client0/login10, A client1/login11, B client2/login12, unrelated login99.
schedule: A reads old metadata without locking and stages login creation
B reads old metadata, chooses replacement, takes its real upsert lock and captures/deletes only seed
B stages seed-login removal; A inserts, commits and acknowledges success while B still owns lock1
B creates its own login, inserts, commits and acknowledges success
completed_counterexample.exact_output: expectedReplica (expectedReplacement seed B) A: old A and new B rows/logins survive with B deployment metadata, seed removed, unrelated login/frame preserved; both responses success, free lock, actual commit IDs [0,1]. This unchecked addition of A is not the sequential operation for A.
completed_counterexample.refutation: Derive the independent sequential fold from actual commit event IDs. Its A-then-B result has no A registration, but the actual result has A. Therefore SerialHistory cannot hold for these actual events and final state.
completed_counterexample.scope: Refutes the defined actual-commit-order contract; no separate all-alternative-orders theorem is claimed.

fixed_protocol: Every reached committing attempt stages the complete ordered admission/replacement program.
Active attempts own the deployment lock exclusively; their metadata observations and captured replacement rows still describe the current committed database.
Each reached commit equals the independent sequential operation for its original request; every finite fixed-protocol execution follows its actual server-commit order.
Aborted attempt identities never appear in the actual commit trace.

Constructed well-formed executions admit replicas, complete overlapping same-metadata requests, replace on changed ordinary metadata, replace unconditionally for instances including equal metadata, and abort after private writes with exact outputs.

native_component_evidence.result: Original actual-store schedule failed; the unchanged regression passed after deployment SELECT FOR UPDATE. Six existing instance-registration integration tests, formatting and strict library Clippy passed. No native checks were repeated for these proof-only changes.

development_notes: The first completed-counterexample check exited1 in35.89s on proof-local state aliases and row-equality elimination; its audit rejected the resulting unfinished theorem. No runtime/model/specification change was used to repair it.
The successful direct run was preceded by a missing-file copy error before any Lean process started. The hash-verified source was transferred, then the check ran once.
The earlier resource-limited prefix construction and repair are recorded in original-midpoint.json; they are not semantic fault-control evidence.

Final Model/Specification edits clarify only comments: full captured rows are proof-level witnesses, native RETURNING fields are client_id/server/login, and external namespace-claim admission does not prohibit arbitrary admitted instance metadata keys.
Existing unused section-variable, simp-argument and unreachable-tactic warnings remain; audited theorem closures contain only the recorded standard axioms.
limits: One retained deployment with namespace-claim ownership and admitted requests supplied externally; only register/replace writers and explicitly disjoint frame changes are modeled.

PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED visibility, transactional atomicity, locking and constraint semantics, Core role/schema internals, native metadata comparison/projection and async Rust/SQL correspondence remain explicit boundaries.
Successful acknowledgement does not imply a registration survives later replacement. A modeled server abort is not inferred from a client transport error.
Constructed traces show reachability, not unconditional progress, physical durability, HTTP or deployed liveness.
Initial deployment creation, RFC7592 per-client update, removal/housekeeping, namespace-claim changes, external-database preparation and postcommit audit/catalog adoption remain broader obligations.
No new runtime authorization rule, proof service, CI hook, deployment, paid model/provider call or full Mac/Linux Docker push gate in this milestone.
